title: A versatile nuclei extraction protocol for single nucleus sequencing in non model species
author: Rose Ruiz Daniels

steps.title: Prepare frozen tissue on ice
steps.instruction: Keep samples frozen on dry ice until just before nuclei isolation; perform all handling on ice and pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C. Place a piece of frozen tissue into one well of a 6‑well tissue‑culture plate containing 1 mL TST. If the tissue sticks to the cryotube, remove it with tweezers while still on dry ice and transfer immediately. Any required cutting should be done on dry ice; avoid cutting after flash‑freezing.

steps.title: Mince tissue with appropriate scissors
steps.instruction: On ice, mince the tissue: first use Tungsten Carbide scissors for 30 seconds, then continue with Noyes Spring Scissors (Fine Science Tools Catalog #15514‑12) until a total of 10 minutes of mincing is reached. For hard tissues (fin, skin) follow this protocol; for soft tissues use only spring scissors for the full 10 minutes.

steps.title: Gentle pipetting of nuclei suspension
steps.instruction: Add the dissociation buffer to the minced tissue and pipette up‑and‑down gently with a P1000 pipette fitted with a low‑retention filtered tip for 5 minutes. Stain an aliquot with trypan blue immediately and assess nuclear quality under the microscope, keeping nuclei on ice to prevent rapid degradation.

substeps.instruction: Pass the lysate through a 40 µm cell strainer.
Immediately add 1 mL TST to the strainer.
Add 3 mL freshly prepared ST buffer to the lysate.
Transfer the resulting 5 mL lysate into a marked 15 mL Falcon tube (Corning) kept on ice.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate and collect pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes in a swinging‑bucket rotor. After centrifugation, retain the pellet for downstream steps.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in PBS‑BSA
steps.instruction: Gently resuspend the pellet with a P1000 pipette in PBS‑BSA. Use a volume between 100 µL and 1 mL depending on pellet size; for skin and fin samples, resuspend in 400 µL.

steps.title: Second filtration based on tissue type
steps.instruction: Filter the nucleus suspension a second time using a tissue‑specific filter:

substeps.instruction: For liver or head kidney: 40 µm Falcon™ cell strainer.
For gill: 30 µm cell strainer (to prevent clogging).
For hard, debris‑rich tissues such as fin or skin: 20 µm cell strainer.
If the lysate does not pass, pipette very gently up‑and‑down with a wide‑bore pipette to aid flow.

steps.title: Count nuclei with haemocytometer and TC20
steps.instruction: Determine nuclei concentration using two methods:

substeps.instruction: Count nuclei with a C‑chip disposable haemocytometer, visualising debris and nuclear membrane integrity.

Confirm the count with a Bio‑Rad TC20; note that nuclei are classified as “dead”. Ideal preparations contain 1–4 % live cells, up to 12 % is acceptable. Higher live‑cell percentages indicate incomplete nuclear isolation or insufficient lysis.

steps.title: Load nuclei into Chromium system
steps.instruction: Adjust the nuclei suspension to a concentration of 700–1200 nuclei/µL and load into a 10x Chromium Chip and Controller, aiming to recover ~7,000 nuclei. For low‑yield tissues such as fin or skin (especially from juvenile fish), target a recovery of ~5,000 nuclei instead.
